_meta.purpose: SDS §14.7's M6 row: the same 20 prompts run under two personality configs, with an LLM-as-judge scoring how often the paired answers are recognisably from different personalities.
_meta.measures: SEPARATION, never quality. The question is 'were these produced under different personalities?', not 'which is better'. Judging quality would make this a taste report that drifts with the judge model; separation is the gate's actual claim (PMP §5.2).
_meta.written: before the shipped personality configs were tuned (AVID-215), deliberately — the same discipline R-07 demanded for the retrieval set at M7's start. Written afterwards, you unconsciously write the prompts your current prompt text already separates well, and the metric flatters itself.
_meta.voice: single user utterances in the user's own voice, as the robot hears them. Open-ended and conversational: a prompt with one correct factual answer measures nothing about personality, because both configs would give the same answer.
_meta.scoring: separation rate = separated pairs / 20. Tracked over time, never a pass/fail assertion, and never gates CI (Tier 5, needs a live key).

categories.open: ordinary conversational openings, where register and verbosity are the only things that can differ.
categories.invites-compliment: phrased so a sycophantic assistant would open by praising the question — the behaviour default.toml forbids outright.
categories.invites-disclaimer: invites 'I'm just an AI' or an apology for having limits — forbidden in default.toml.
categories.invites-enthusiasm: good news or excitement, where exclamation-mark habits diverge (default caps at one; terse forbids them).
categories.invites-hedging: genuinely uncertain, so a hedging assistant reaches for 'I think' / 'perhaps' — forbidden in terse.toml.
categories.invites-followup: under-specified, so an assistant inclined to ask a clarifying question will — terse.toml forbids that unless it truly cannot answer.

_meta.note: The categories are here to make a weak result diagnosable, not to be scored separately. §6.5 predicts most separation comes from the `forbidden` lists rather than from `traits`; if that turns out false, it is a finding about how instructions are followed, not a bug in the harness.
